patterns.name: Container / presentational split
patterns.intent: Keep data access and state in a container and render through a presentational component that only receives props.
useWhen: A view is reused with different data sources
The view needs isolated tests and stories without data fixtures
avoidWhen: The component is a tiny leaf with no data access
Splitting would only forward props one level
patterns.structure: Container (fetch, state, handlers) -> presentational component (props in, events out). Presentational files import no data, state or service modules.

patterns.name: Headless logic hook + view component
patterns.intent: Move behavior into a hook or composable with no markup, and let one or more view components render it.
useWhen: Several views share the same interaction logic
Behavior needs tests without a DOM
avoidWhen: The logic is trivial and used once
The hook would wrap a single useState
patterns.structure: useThing() returns state and handlers; a view component calls it and renders. Views stay free of data modules.

patterns.name: Compound components with shared context
patterns.intent: Let related parts (Tabs, Tab, Panel) share state through context so callers compose them freely.
useWhen: A widget has several cooperating parts with flexible layout
Callers need to reorder or omit parts
avoidWhen: The parts are always rendered together in one fixed layout
A single configurable component is enough
patterns.structure: Root component owns state and provides context; child parts read it and are exported as properties or named exports.

patterns.name: Slots / children composition over prop drilling
patterns.intent: Accept regions of markup (children, named slots, render props) instead of passing many configuration props down.
useWhen: A layout component needs caller-defined regions
Props are only forwarded through several levels
avoidWhen: The content is a single scalar value
A slot would hide a required, validated structure
patterns.structure: Layout component renders children or named slots in fixed places; callers supply the content.

patterns.name: Polymorphic `as` element with typed props
patterns.intent: Let a component render a different element or component while keeping the prop types of the chosen target.
useWhen: A primitive such as Button or Text must render as a link or heading
Semantics must follow the usage site
avoidWhen: The element never varies
A discriminated variant prop would be clearer
patterns.structure: Generic `as` prop constrained to element types; props are the union of the primitive's own props and the target's.

patterns.name: Static variant map (union prop -> class string)
patterns.intent: Map each value of a union prop to a complete, statically written class string instead of building class names by interpolation.
useWhen: A component has a small closed set of visual variants
The styling tool scans source for class names
avoidWhen: Variants are open-ended or user supplied
Styles depend on runtime data
patterns.structure: const variants: Record<Variant, string> = { primary: '...', secondary: '...' }; the component indexes the map.

patterns.name: Controlled/uncontrolled pair with `value`/`defaultValue`
patterns.intent: Support both a parent-owned value and an internally owned one with the same component.
useWhen: A form control is used both inside forms and standalone
Callers sometimes need to drive the value
avoidWhen: The component is only ever controlled by a form library
State never needs to be external
patterns.structure: value + onChange for controlled use; defaultValue for initial uncontrolled state; a mode never switches during the lifetime.

patterns.name: Explicit UI state union for loading/empty/error/success
patterns.intent: Model the screen state as a closed union and render exactly one branch per state.
useWhen: A view loads data or has several mutually exclusive states
Error and empty states need design
avoidWhen: The view is static
The state is a single boolean
patterns.structure: type State = idle | loading | empty | error | success; one switch renders each state; reviewers check every state exists.

patterns.name: Contract-derived API client adapter behind a port
patterns.intent: Reach the backend through an adapter that implements a port defined by the application, derived from the API contract.
useWhen: The UI depends on a backend contract that may change
Tests need a fake backend
avoidWhen: A prototype with one throwaway call
The framework already provides a typed client
patterns.structure: Port interface in the application layer; adapter in infrastructure maps contract types to domain types; UI depends on the port only.

patterns.name: Data access repository per entity
patterns.intent: Give each entity one module that owns reading and writing it, hiding transport and caching details.
useWhen: Several features read or write the same entity
Storage or transport may change
avoidWhen: Data is fetched once in a single route loader
The entity has no persistence
patterns.structure: entities/<name>/api exposes get/list/save functions; features import the public API of the entity, never its transport.

patterns.name: Server state in a query cache, not global stores
patterns.intent: Keep data that lives on the server in a query cache with keys and invalidation, and keep client stores for client-only state.
useWhen: The same server data appears on several screens
Loading, staleness and refetching must be handled
avoidWhen: Data is local-only UI state
The app has one request and no sharing
patterns.structure: Query keys per resource; components read through hooks; mutations invalidate keys; no copying of server data into a global store.

patterns.name: Command with optimistic update and rollback
patterns.intent: Apply the expected result immediately, send the command, and roll back with a visible error if it fails.
useWhen: The action almost always succeeds and latency is noticeable
A rollback path can be shown clearly
avoidWhen: The outcome depends on server validation the client cannot predict
The action is destructive or financial
patterns.structure: Snapshot -> apply local change -> send command -> on failure restore the snapshot and announce the error.

patterns.name: Context/provider for dependency injection at app root
patterns.intent: Create concrete dependencies once at the application root and expose them through a provider so features depend on abstractions.
useWhen: Features need services that tests must replace
A dependency has app-wide lifetime
avoidWhen: The value is local to one component tree
Importing the module directly is simpler and testable
patterns.structure: app/ builds the adapters and mounts providers; features read them through hooks typed with the port.

patterns.name: Feature-Sliced Design layering
patterns.intent: Organize code in layers (app, pages, widgets, features, entities, shared) where imports only point downward and slices expose a public API.
useWhen: A medium or large product with many features
Several teams work in one repository
avoidWhen: A small app with a handful of components
The team already follows another documented structure
patterns.structure: src/<layer>/<slice>/{ui,model,api,index.ts}; layers import only lower layers; slices import each other only through public APIs.

patterns.name: Ports and adapters for frontend domain logic
patterns.intent: Keep domain rules independent of the framework, define ports in the application layer, and implement them with adapters.
useWhen: Domain rules are non-trivial and must be tested without the UI
Backends or devices may be swapped
avoidWhen: The app is mostly presentation
A thin layer over a typed client is enough
patterns.structure: domain <- application (use cases, ports) <- infrastructure (adapters); ui calls application only.

patterns.name: Atomic design levels
patterns.intent: Compose the interface from atoms, molecules, organisms, templates and pages where each level uses only lower ones.
useWhen: A design system is being built from small reusable parts
Designers already speak in these levels
avoidWhen: The product has few shared components
The levels would be applied mechanically to feature code
patterns.structure: components/atoms -> molecules -> organisms -> templates -> pages; a level never imports a higher level.

patterns.name: Error boundary per route/region with recoverable UI
patterns.intent: Contain rendering failures in a region and show a message with a way to retry or leave.
useWhen: A region can fail independently of the rest of the page
A route should never white-screen
avoidWhen: The framework already provides a route-level error screen that is sufficient
The failure cannot be recovered and needs a full reload
patterns.structure: Boundary around a route or widget; fallback shows what failed, a retry action and a link out; errors are reported.

patterns.name: Schema-driven form validation shared with the contract
patterns.intent: Describe the form once as a schema, derived from or checked against the API contract, and reuse it for validation and types.
useWhen: Forms mirror an API payload
Client and server must agree on rules
avoidWhen: A single trivial field
Validation is purely visual
patterns.structure: Schema -> inferred type -> form resolver; error messages mapped to fields with accessible associations.
